content.completion: Require actual author-intended final narrative and independent raw-output verification. Death, quitting, day/chapter transitions and intermediate scores are insufficient. Do not chase maximum points after a verified ending.
content.dataset_purpose: Synthetic user-command test data, not a player-skill benchmark
content.checkpoint_policy: Save at ordinary command prompts only; confirm engine success. Exit menus before parser commands.

# Collection notes

Curses R16/951024; guide explicitly for1.6/R16. Even with matching release, verify each command against actual output. Long multi-area puzzles: save at milestones and stop after the substantive ending, not a completionist points sweep.

First inspect current startup: answer any key pause or question before saving. Use small broker walkthrough hints. Label synthetic human-like mistakes and verify same-intent recovery effects. Keep coverage varied; do not repeat known failures merely to make more rows. A displayed menu requires its own navigation/exit before ordinary commands. Write progress only to progress.md, never to inbox/*.json; requests must be complete JSON. No training, application changes or publication.

2026-09-25 03:44 UTC menu transport note: MENU INPUT: For a menu that says RETURN or Enter, send an empty command string ("command":""). Do not spell RETURN, ENTER, SPACE or BACKSPACE as words. A literal space ("command":" ") is a different key from Enter. The plain CLI passes the first byte of nonempty input; an empty line sends Return. Menu controls are not ordinary parser commands: consult the actual menu labels. Avoid optional HELP/file menus if collection-notes.md documents stalled transport; request a small broker walkthrough excerpt instead. If output times out, await_output only; never use another key to flush it.

Under the pseudonym Marie Swelldon, your ancestress Alison (1871-1930) wrote 
several mildly successful romances. She obsessively collected lucky charms, and 
advertised in newspapers for double-headed coins and the like (although she 
never traced a rumoured find of a five-leafed clover, somewhere in County 
Donegal).

In order to write in tranquillity and to avoid her husband, it was she who 
installed the fake wall at the far south end of the attic east wing, and each 
afternoon she would sneak upstairs to push it aside.

wore jewelled buttons worth at least a thousand pounds) and for marrying a lady

to be beheaded. In order to stop his sister getting the fortune, he went back 
to Italy and advertised for a pregnant bride to provide a male heir. This 
nefarious plot was foiled when he choked to death on a chicken-bone.

In 1792, the last year of his life, ol' red-eyes becomes very excited about his 
new discovery. This time he claims that Merlyn bounde uppe the mystic estate 
(by this he means the back garden - Isaac never did have any sense of 
proportion) wyth great Roddes of Power. These are dangerous, yet also useful in 
themselves, but are really part of a great key... the usual nonsense. Of course 
you never actually see these rods, because they disguise themselves until waved 
by someone wearing Merlyn's hat.

only a week after this breakthrough, preventing him from sending yet another 
paper to the Royal Society. But since Merlyn supposedly lived in about the 
sixth century A.D., there can't be a lot left of his hat, so the matter may be

the timer in the flash. Close the flash. Put the flash in the device.
Wait until the timer goes off. E, E. Lagach the mosaic and keep
`lagaching' until you get back to the frieze. U. Take all.

Aunt Jemima's Lair
This used to be called the Conservatory, before Aunt Jemima took it over to 
potter about with plants, painting and indeed (on occasion) pottery. She has 
filled the place with objets trouves and bric-a-brac, and hung up a home-made 
calendar of watercolours. Even the old airing cupboard to the south is 
cluttered.

An open doorway leads back southwest onto the upstairs landing, and you can 
hear the chaotic noise of suitcases being manhandled about - good thing 
nobody's seen you. A narrow staircase leads up and to the east into the attic.

Jemima herself seems to be in the potting room to the west.

The wireless fills the air with Jemima's favourite station, "Mild-n-Breezy FM", 
about which the least said the better.

The radio plays a synthesized rendition of Ian Dury and the Blockheads' "Hit Me 
With Your Rhythm Stick".
